Role: fault localization only; project source and tests unchanged.
Findings:
- src/components/views/elements/Pill.tsx is a default-exported class. load() combines URL parsing, entity lookup, async profile fetch, and state; render() combines type-specific text/avatar/class decisions, tooltip, and link behavior. A valid-looking message URL can throw because parsePermalink(url) may return null before parts.primaryEntityId is read. The user branch sets href=null and replaces missing display names with "", so it loses the input URL and can show empty text instead of the MXID. Explicit @room with no room can produce a classless pill because pillType is set even without room.
- src/utils/pillify.tsx imports default Pill and calls Pill.roomNotifPos/roomNotifLen; src/components/views/elements/ReplyChain.tsx and settings/BridgeTile.tsx also import the default. These need named imports when the public surface changes.
- src/utils/permalinks/Permalinks.ts exports getPrimaryPermalinkEntity and parsePermalink. The latter returns null for unsupported URLs. The existing code chooses parsePermalink for inMessage and getPrimaryPermalinkEntity otherwise; parsing should only determine identity, preserving the exact incoming href.
- Existing coverage: test/utils/pillify-test.tsx checks @room conversion and repeated calls; test/components/views/messages/TextualBody-test.tsx checks user and room DOM, avatars, and room URL including via parameters. No dedicated Pill/usePermalink tests found.
Uncertainty: expected treatment of explicit user/room type without a URL is not fully defined beyond fail-quiet and @room; the hook should avoid deriving an ID without a resolvable URL.
